title: NY State Assembly · District 26
area: Northeast Queens, including Bayside, Douglaston, Little Neck, Auburndale and parts of Flushing and Whitestone.

context.text: Incumbent Edward Braunstein advanced from the Democratic primary without appearing on the ballot. Robert Speranza defeated Philip Grillo 61.5%-37.8% in the June 23, 2026 Republican primary to again face Braunstein, whom he also ran against in 2022 and 2024.

summary.text: Edward Braunstein is the Democratic incumbent for NY State Assembly District 26, first elected in 2010. He chairs the Assembly Corporations, Authorities and Commissions Committee, which oversees utility and public-authority regulation, and also serves on the Health, Judiciary, Rules and Ways and Means committees.

background.text: Earned a B.S. in Finance from the State University of New York at Albany in 2003 and a J.D. from New York Law School in 2008.
Worked as a legislative assistant to Assembly Speaker Sheldon Silver before his own election.
Served on Community Board 11, which covers Northeast Queens neighborhoods.

positions.summary: Sponsored A02047, creating a real-property tax abatement and exemption for capital improvements that reduce carbon emissions, with co-sponsors including David Weprin and Nily Rozic.

record.text: Chairs the Assembly Corporations, Authorities and Commissions Committee (2025-2026), which has jurisdiction over the Public Service Commission and utility regulation; also serves on the Health, Judiciary, Rules, and Ways and Means committees. Previously chaired the Cities Committee (2021-2024).

Sponsored A08675 ("prevention of damage to critical infrastructure act"), restricting junk and scrap dealers from buying metals used by critical infrastructure providers; passed the Assembly on March 9, 2026, amended and repassed May 18, 2026, and was substituted into and enacted as part of Senate bill S8302-D by June 4, 2026.

Sponsored A10422, requiring that any Public Service Commission sanction or civil penalty against a utility be returned to ratepayers as a direct bill credit within 90 days; passed the Assembly on June 4, 2026 after being substituted for companion bill S8908.

Sponsored A02429, directing the Department of Public Service to report on the affordability of water services for residential and commercial customers; referred to the Corporations, Authorities and Commissions Committee, not enacted as of January 2026.
Sponsored A02047, establishing a property-tax abatement and exemption for capital improvements that reduce carbon emissions; referred to committee, not enacted as of this writing.
Voted yes on S10113, allowing a cannabis microbusiness licensee to conduct retail sales, which passed the Assembly 88-53 on June 5, 2026.
Voted yes on S3460, granting employees access to their personnel records, which passed the Assembly 92-49 on May 19, 2026.

candidates.name: Robert Speranza

summary.text: Robert Speranza is the Republican nominee for NY State Assembly District 26, defeating Philip Grillo in the June 2026 Republican primary. He previously ran against incumbent Edward Braunstein in the 2022 and 2024 general elections, losing both.

candidates.researchNotes: No campaign website, Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey response for 2026 or prior cycles, or reported campaign-finance activity ($0 contributions and expenditures in 2022 and 2024 per OpenSecrets/FEC data cited on Ballotpedia) could be found.

researchNotes: Braunstein's committee chairmanship and bill-status details are drawn from official NY Assembly pages. Speranza has run in this district three consecutive cycles but has almost no independently documented public record or reported campaign activity.
